title: Redundant Doc-Comment Restating Signature
pattern: Doc-comment list of arguments that merely repeats the names and types of function parameters with no added constraints or units.
why_bad: Boilerplate clutter that dilutes the actual code and creates a high risk of stale documentation when signatures are refactored.
detection: Documentation comments on parameter arguments where the description contains only the parameter name, type, or trivial conversions thereof (e.g., parameter `title` documented as 'The title').
counterexample: Parameter documentation stating constraints not visible in the signature, such as units, valid ranges, or ownership rules (e.g., '`duration` - playback length in whole minutes; must be non-zero').
fix: Delete the explicit parameter boilerplate; document only high-level behavior or exceptional invariants in a single cohesive paragraph.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Bad Comments - Redundant Comments"); Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020), Chapter 10.2 ("Documentation Types").
